title: 5.0L 32V Ti-VCT Cooling Component Map
introduction:
I use this drawing as a plumbing map for the engine’s heat-delivery network. The radiator is at the left, the engine block and cylinder heads are at the right, and the heater-core branch stretches across the upper right. The degas bottle sits above the radiator area, while the oil-cooler branch appears below the engine. Those branches explain why the cooling system is more than a pair of big radiator hoses.

Choose a component in the drawing, follow its callout line, and match its item label to the accompanying table. To trace a route, follow the small arrowheads and the thin connecting lines across the gaps between separated parts. The colors show temperature bands within the coolant circuit; they do not identify different fluids. The oil filter appears beside the cooler and adapter for location context, not as a coolant passage.

This is an identification and illustrated-flow reference. The separated layout is not an access or removal sequence, and its temperature colors are not diagnostic pass/fail limits. Filling, bleeding, opening connections and testing require their matching procedures.

edits.text: NOTE: Coolant temperature changes with ambient temperature and engine load. This drawing uses an ambient temperature of 38° C (100° F). Red arrows show coolant over 82.2° C (180° F); orange arrows show coolant at approximately 82.2° C (180° F); blue arrows show coolant below 82.2° C (180° F).
edits.why: Use the colors to compare the illustrated routes under the stated conditions. They are temperature bands, not universal overheating thresholds or proof of a component fault.
